outcome: Phase 3 step 3 of the latency plan: after an enrollment rule change the runtime reuses the serialized rows of candidates whose decisions did not change instead of re-evaluating and re-serializing all 5,785 of them. On the household installation the catalog block of a save fell from a median 0.81 s to 0.11 s, the evaluation from 1.59 s to 0.86 s, the server save total from 2.68 s to 1.96 s, the client save response from 3.23 s to 2.20 s and the settled panel from 3.35 s to 2.38 s. A save without a collector pause now takes about 1.5 s on the server; every Stop in this run still contained one generation-2 collection of about 0.85 s and every Resume did not.
plan: Homeostatic save and refresh latency investigation plan, phase 3 step 3 (fix by measured share with a live before and after)

status.code_changes: custom_components/homeostatic/enrollment.py: report() accepts already-evaluated sources and previous rows and reuses a row when its source is unchanged; custom_components/homeostatic/runtime.py: the catalog rebuild passes the evaluated candidates, the previous candidates and the published rows. tests/test_candidate_row_reuse.py: an exclusion edit serializes exactly one candidate row and reuses the rest as the same objects, the delta carries exactly that row, a fresh report equals the patched rows by key, and excluding many candidates regenerates exactly those rows.

ranking_for_the_next_change: Garbage collection: with the catalog block gone, a 0.85 s generation-2 collection is now a third of a Stop; lower the allocation churn around saves (snapshot, read-back and compare on every refresh, checkpoint deep copies) and debounce saves
Discovery (0.47 s on every save and once a minute): run it on registry, config-entry and repairs events with a slow safety reconcile
The remaining fixed costs of a save are checkpoint 0.12 s, snapshot 0.15 s, storage about 0.2 s and completion 0.3 s
